reason: C3 is chosen because it proposes a concrete intervention (stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations, SCCPs) that is specific to high-entropy alloys (HEAs) and gives a mechanism (dislocation transmission and stress relief) that is physically consistent and derived from materials-science principles. The hypothesis also makes quantified predictions (ultrahigh strength >2 GPa and ductility >10%) and has a decisive falsification test (tensile testing and microstructural analysis of HEAs with and without SCCPs). Additionally, C3 provides a clear structural mediator (coherent nanoprecipitations) and boundaries (high-temperature conditions up to 800 °C and ambient temperature), which further supports its selection as the best candidate.
